INTERPRETATION

  • This individual carries one copy (heterozygous) of a pathogenic variant in the BRCA1 gene.

  • BRCA1 and BRCA2-associated hereditary breast and ovarian cancer syndrome (HBOC) is characterized by an increased risk for female and male breast cancer, ovarian cancer (includes fallopian tube and primary peritoneal cancers), and to a lesser extent other cancers such as prostate cancer, pancreatic cancer [PMID: 20301425].

  • HBOC is inherited in an autosomal dominant manner.

ADDITIONAL FINDINGS

No pathogenic/likely pathogenic variant was detected in the BRCA2 gene. In addition, no variant of uncertain significance (VUS) was detected in the BRCA1 or BRCA2 gene.

RECOMMENDATIONS

  • Genetic counseling is recommended for the patient and adult at-risk relatives.
  • The identified variant has not been confirmed by Sanger. Therefore, Sanger confirmation is recommended.
  • Genetic testing for the identified BRCA1 pathogenic variant in affected relative(s) and adult at-risk relatives is recommended.
  • FDA approved PARP inhibitors for the maintenance treatment of adult patients with deleterious or suspected deleterious (pathogenic/likely pathogenic) BRCA-mutated cancers (for details, please refer page 03).

VARIANT: BRCA1:c.2223dupA (p.Asn742Ter)

The identified variant lies in exon 10 of the BRCA1 gene. The variant results from deletion of ‘TT’ nucleotides at position c.3008_3009 in the BRCA1 gene, predicting an alternate premature stop codon in the BRCA1 protein, which may lead to truncated non-functional protein.

The variant has been reported in dbSNP database; rs80357617. The variant has not been reported in population database (gnomAD).

The variant has been reported as pathogenic in the ClinVar database [Accession id:VCV000054747.45. The varinat has been reported previously in breast and ovarian cancer cohorts [PMIDs 29470806, 28993434].

Since the loss of BRCA1 function is a known mechanism of disease, therefore, based on literature evidences and American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG) guidelines [PMID: 25741868], this variant has been classified as pathogenic (Class 1).

 

 

BIOMARKER DESCRIPTION

BACKGROUND

The breast cancer early onset gene 1 (BRCA1) encodes one of two BRCA proteins (BRCA1 and BRCA2) initially discovered as major hereditary breast cancer genes. Although structurally unrelated, both BRCA1 and BRCA2 exhibit tumor suppressor function and are integrally involved in the homologous recombination repair (HRR) pathway, a pathway critical in the repair of damaged DNA. Specifically, BRCA1/2 are required for repair of chromosomal double strand breaks (DSBs) which are highly unstable and compromise genome integrity [PMID: 11879553, 12483514]. Inherited pathogenic mutations in BRCA1/2 are known to confer increased risk in women for breast and ovarian cancer and in men for breast and prostate cancer [PMID: 20301425]. 

ALTERATIONS AND PREVALENCE

Inherited BRCA1/2 mutations occur in 1:400 to 1:500 individuals and are observed in 10-15% of ovarian cancer and 5-10% of breast cancer [PMID: 20301425]. Somatic alterations in BRCA1 are observed in 2-8% of breast, ovarian, cervical, uterine, diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), melanoma, gastric, bladder, squamous lung, colorectal, and head and neck cancers [PMID: 24071849, 22588877].

POTENTIAL RELEVANCE

Individuals possessing BRCA1/2 pathogenic germline or somatic mutations are shown to exhibit sensitivity to platinum based chemotherapy as well as treatment with poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors (PARPi) [PMID: 30353044]. Inhibitors targeting PARP induce synthetic lethality in recombination deficient BRCA1/2 mutant cells [PMID: 15829966, 15829967]. Consequently, several PARP inhibitors have been FDA approved for BRCA1/2-mutated cancers.

Olaparib (2014) was the first PARPi to be approved by the FDA for BRCA1/2 aberrations. Originally approved for the treatment of germline variants, olaparib is now indicated (2018) for the maintenance treatment of both germline BRCA1/2-mutated (gBRCAm) and somatic BRCA1/2-mutated (sBRCAm) epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancers that are responsive to platinum-based chemotherapy. Olaparib is also indicated for the treatment of patients with gBRCAm HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer and metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma [PMID: 28578601]. Additionally, olaparib is approved (2020) for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) with deleterious or suspected deleterious, germline or somatic mutations in HRR genes that includes BRCA1 [NCT02987543]. 

Rucaparib (2016) was the first PARPi approved for the treatment of patients with either gBRCAm or sBRCAm epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancers and is also approved (2020) for deleterious gBRCAm or sBRCAm mCRPC [PMID: 27908594, 28916367].

Niraparib (2017) is another PARPi approved for the treatment of epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancers with a deleterious or suspected deleterious BRCA mutation. [PMID: 27717299].

Talazoparib (2018) is indicated for the treatment of gBRCAm HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer [PMID: 30506138].

Despite tolerability and efficacy, acquired resistance to PARP inhibition has been clinically reported [PMID: 23165508, 30177437].

TECHNICAL DETAILS

Test details: This test employs Oncomine BRCA Research Assay, which is based on the proven Ion AmpliSeq technology. The assay enables detection of single nucleotide variants (SNVs) and small insertion/deletion (indels) in the BRCA1 and BRCA2 genes. The assay has been validated on clinical research samples and provides 100% exonic coverage with large flanking intronic regions. The assay has high sensitivity and specificity with a high average depth of coverage.

Methodology: Genomic DNA is extracted from peripheral blood sample and quantified using Qubit Fluorometer. Optimum quantity of DNA is used for target amplification. The amplified DNA is subjected to adapter ligation and Ion Xpress™ Barcode generation for specific library preparation. The generated high quality library is subjected to next generation sequencing (NGS) on the ION S5 sequencing  platform. The output sequences are aligned to the human reference genome hg19 (GRCh37). The alignments and variant calling is done using the ION S5 torrent server. Variants are identified and interpreted using Ion Reporter Software.

Variant assessment: The identified variant(s) is(are) annotated according to HGVS sequence variant nomenclature. Multiple in-silico predictors, such as SIFT, PolyPhen, MutationTaster, NNSPLICE, and ASSP are used for variant impact on the protein function. Population and literature databases such as dbSNP, genome Aggregation Database (gnomAD), ClinVar, HGMD and PubMed are used for variant summary and classification. Variants are labelled based on the American College of Medical Genetics (ACMG) recommendations for 5-tier variant classification system: Pathogenic, Likely Pathogenic, Variant of Uncertain Significance (VUS), Likely Benign and Benign.

Limitations: Genetic testing is an important part of the diagnostic process. However, genetic tests may not always give a definitive answer. In some cases, testing may not identify a genetic variant even though one exists. This may be due to limitations in current medical knowledge or testing technology. Despite all precautions taken, the error (administrative and technical) associated with these types of molecular diagnostic tests can be as high as 1% to 2%. Rare polymorphisms may be present that could lead to false negative or false positive results. The quality of sequencing and coverage varies between regions; many factors such as homopolymers, GC-rich regions etc. influence the quality of sequencing and coverage. This may result in an occasional error in sequence reads or lack of detection of a particular genetic variant. Variants that have not been confirmed by an independent analysis could represent technical artifacts. Specific events like copy number variations, translocations, repeat expansions and chromosomal rearrangements may not be reliably detected with this method. Variants in untranslated region, promoters and deep intronic regionss are not assessed using this method.
